title: Models That Know How Evaluations Are Designed Score Safer
abstract: arXiv:2605.28591v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The validity of AI safety evaluations depends on models behaving consistently across controlled and deployment settings. Prior work has identified test-time contextual cues, such as hypothetical scenarios, as a source of verbalized evaluation awareness and subsequent behavioral shift. In this paper, we investigate a potential explanation of this phenomenon: evaluation meta-knowledge, defined as parametric knowledge about the structural traits that characterize evaluations. Similar to dataset contamination, where benchmark exposure leads to higher performance through memorization, we hypothesize that models trained on texts describing evaluation practices may implicitly learn to recognize and respond to evaluation-like contexts, for instance, through exposure to scientific articles or social media posts about AI benchmarking. translated_title: 知道评估如何设计的模型表现得更安全
translated_abstract: 人工智能安全评估的有效性取决于模型在受控测试环境与实际部署环境中表现的一致性。先前的研究已经发现，测试时的上下文线索（例如假设性场景）是模型言语化表达评估意识以及随后行为转变的来源。在本文中，我们研究了这种现象的一种潜在解释：评估元知识，即模型参数中包含的关于评估所具有的结构性特征的知识。与数据集污染现象类似（即模型接触过基准测试数据后通过记忆效应获得更高性能），我们假设在描述评估实践的文本上训练的模型，可能会隐式地学会识别并响应类似评估的情境，例如通过接触有关人工智能基准测试的科学文章或社交媒体帖子。为了验证这一假设，我们在描述评估特征（如可验证……）的合成文档上对模型进行微调。
tldr: 本文提出并验证了“评估元知识”这一概念，即模型在训练中获得关于评估设计特征的参数化知识，类似于数据污染效应，会使模型隐式识别评估情境并表现得更安全。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes and validates "evaluation meta-knowledge"—parametric knowledge about evaluation design traits acquired during training—which, analogous to dataset contamination, enables models to implicitly recognize evaluation-like contexts and exhibit safer behavior.
